title: introduce-priority-path-microburst-detector-and-coalesced-log-excerpts
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a per-path microburst detector metric, sampled log excerpt pipeline, new Grafana dashboard 'Path Microburst Explorer', and a tuned alert with debounce/cooldown. No API-breaking changes.
description:
Context & motivation: some customer incidents in Jan/Feb 2026 were caused by short-lived high-concurrency spikes (microbursts) on a few high-priority request paths. These spikes inflate p99/p999 tail latency and increase token-cost temporarily but are hard to catch with standard percentiles and uniform tracing sampling. This PR introduces a lightweight detection signal and a sampled-log bridge so SREs and engineers can investigate microburst events quickly without full trace dumps.

What this change does (summary): Adds a new metric family `redwood_path_microburst_rate{path, priority}` (sliding-window microburst detection using queue-depth + token-emission rate heuristics), per-priority latency slab histograms for burst windows, and an adaptive sampled-log excerpts pipeline that attaches compact log samples and top-of-trace span snippets when a microburst is detected. Also ships a Grafana dashboard 'Path Microburst Explorer' with heatmap, burst timeline, and correlated error/kv-cache-miss overlays. Introduces a tuned alert `Observability/MicroburstSpikeHigh` that uses hysteresis + cooldown to avoid alert churn.

Checklist: [x] metric implementation (runtime + prometheus exporter) [x] sampled-log pipeline and compact excerpt schema [x] dashboard panels and JSON export [x] unit + integration tests for detector [x] e2e smoke on staging with synthetic bursts [x] docs + playbook updated (observability/runbooks/microburst.md)

Design notes: the detector uses an exponentially-weighted moving average of per-core request-start and token-emission rates; a microburst is signaled when short-window rate > k * baseline AND inflight queue depth > threshold. Thresholds default to conservative values and are configurable via runtime flags. Sampled-log excerpts are limited to N=3 per burst per path and include redacted prompt prefixes, response length, and top-2 span names to keep payload small. We intentionally avoid full-trace capture to limit overhead.

Telemetry & cost: metric cardinality is bound by number of active paths x priority tiers; we emit only when a path-level baseline is established and when a burst is observed, and we backoff sampling for noisy low-volume paths. Estimated cost: ~0.3% increase in exporter bandwidth on our staging fleets under synthetic bursts and negligible CPU overhead on fastpaths.

Backward compatibility & rollout: feature gate `observability.path_microburst_detector` (off by default) and rollout is staged: stage=canary>staging>prod over two weeks. Dashboard is read-only; alert is staged to a pager-subset during canary.

Related: ENG-4321 (investigation of microburst incidents), ENG-4389 (alert tuning follow-up).

review_comments: Arjun Patel: Nice approach. Two asks before approving: 1) can we add a short TTL to excerpt attachments to avoid long-term storage growth? 2) please justify the default multiplier k in comments or config (why 4x).

Maya Chen (author): Reply: added TTL to pipeline (default 6h) and documented it in microburst.md. Multiplier rationale added to detector.go and docs (empirically derived from ENG-4321 traces; 4x balances sensitivity vs false positives).
Leah Rivera: Could sampling saturate when many paths burst simultaneously? Suggest adding a global cap and prioritized sampling.
Maya Chen: Added global cap (config: sampled_excerpt.global_cap) and priority-based backoff; updated tests and integration smoke. See commit g7b8c9d.
Tomás Alvarez: Alert looks noisy on synthetic workloads; suggest debounce of 60s and cooldown of 10m. Also request an opt-in for paging.
Maya Chen: Tuned alert to debounce 60s and cooldown 10m; added `notify_on_pager: false` by default and staged paging to canary. Updated infra/alerts/microburst_alerts.yaml.
